title: Do Not Forget In the Good Times

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: When the Lord your God brings you into the land he swore to your fathers, to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, to give you—a land with large, flourishing cities you did not build, houses filled with all kinds of good things you did not provide, wells you did not dig, and vineyards and olive groves you did not plant—then when you eat and are satisfied, be careful that you do not forget the Lord, who brought you out of Egypt, out of the land of slavery. - Deut 6:10-12 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God warns His people about a surprising danger — not hardship, but blessing. When they entered the land and enjoyed cities, houses, wells, and vineyards they had not worked for, the temptation would be to forget the Giver in the enjoyment of the gifts. Prosperity has a way of dulling our memory. In our struggles we cry out to God; in our comfort we can quietly drift from Him.

This is one of the most honest warnings in Scripture about the human heart. Notice that everything good in the land was a gift — cities they did not build, wells they did not dig. It was all grace. Yet the danger was that satisfied people would begin to think they had earned it, or simply forget the One who provided it. Full stomachs and comfortable lives can make us spiritually forgetful and self-sufficient.

We must guard our hearts in the good times as carefully as in the hard times. Every good gift comes from God (Jas 1:17), and the proper response to blessing is deeper gratitude and dependence, not forgetfulness. This is worlds away from a prosperity mindset that treats blessing as a reward we deserve. Instead, when life is good, let it drive you back to the Giver with thanksgiving. Remember the Lord who rescued you, and never let His gifts crowd out the Giver Himself.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Am I more prone to seek God in hardship and forget Him in comfort?
- Do I recognise the good things in my life as gifts from God's hand?
- How can I let blessings lead me to deeper gratitude rather than forgetfulness?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, guard my heart in times of blessing, that I would never forget You who gives every good gift. Keep me grateful and dependent, remembering that all I have comes from Your hand. Amen.
